issues.description: signing_mode_enum function has implicit fallthrough that could mask logic errors
issues.detail: The free function signing_mode_enum() in wallet_request_types.py covers three explicit if/elif cases and falls through to CHIP_0002 for the remaining case (not is_hex and safe_mode). While the truth-table is exhaustive for bools, the implicit fallthrough is hard to audit. Make the final case explicit (elif not is_hex and safe_mode) and add an assertion/raise for unreachable, to prevent silent miscategorization if the input types ever change.

issues.description: verify_signature raises ValueError for unknown signing modes instead of returning a response
issues.detail: In chia/wallet/util/signing.py, the else branch raises ValueError(f"Unsupported signing mode: {signing_mode!r}"). The original RPC behavior raised on string parsing, but here signing_mode is already a SigningMode enum, so this branch is logically dead unless the enum is extended. Either remove the branch with assert_never, or document the invariant — currently it suggests a runtime-reachable path that would surface as a 500 instead of a structured VerifySignatureResponse.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic on main_wallet used for DID/NFT keys conflates wallet identity
issues.detail: sign_message_by_id now calls self.service.wallet_state_manager.main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(...) with a private key fetched for the DID/NFT p2 puzzle hash. The synthetic conversion uses DEFAULT_HIDDEN_PUZZLE_HASH which is a constant, so result is correct, but routing through main_wallet creates a misleading coupling. Extract convert_secret_key_to_synthetic as a module-level helper (or static method) in signing.py to avoid implying main_wallet ownership of the key.

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address never asserts the verification result
issues.detail: In test_wallet_rpc.py, test_sign_message_by_address calls verify_signature but discards the return value. If verify_signature returns isValid=False with an error, the test still passes. Capture the response and assert response.isValid is True. Currently this test only exercises that the call doesn't raise, which is much weaker than the comment 'adds tests for the previously untested sign_message_by_id' implies.

issues.description: Stale docstring left in verify_signature helper
issues.detail: The new verify_signature() in chia/wallet/util/signing.py keeps the docstring ':param request:\n:return:' from the old RPC method, but the function no longer takes a request object — it takes individual keyword args. Update the docstring to reflect the new signature, or drop it. Minor, but the file is the canonical home for this logic now.

issues.description: Duplicate signing_mode_enum name (free function and property) hurts readability
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py defines a module-level function signing_mode_enum and also adds .signing_mode_enum properties on VerifySignature/SignMessageByAddress/SignMessageByID that delegate to it. Two namespaces with the same name plus a property that wraps a free function makes navigation harder. Rename the free function (e.g., _signing_mode_from_flags) to make the relationship explicit.

review.summary: The refactor cleanly consolidates duplicated signing/verification logic from three wallets and the RPC into chia/wallet/util/signing.py — a clear win for maintainability. Main concerns: (1) signing_mode_enum() relies on implicit fallthrough for the CHIP_0002 case, (2) the new verify_signature has an unreachable-by-type ValueError path that would surface as a 500, (3) routing DID/NFT key conversion through main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is misleading since it's effectively a pure function, and (4) test_sign_message_by_address never asserts the verify response is valid. No P0 correctness or security issues found; the signing math appears preserved verbatim.
